messages:
Sam (AE): Hey team — running a presales POC with FinBank EU. They asked for a clear runbook about network egress and our transport/cert stack, and whether any traffic can traverse non-EU sub-processors. Also need to confirm any egress charging implications. Can ops/infra/ legal weigh in?
Ben (Solutions): +1, can you paste the customer's Qs? short list will help. also: are they on Hosted API or asking about Dedicated/Private?
Sam (AE): Hosted API for now, but they want an option to move to Dedicated later. Customer Qs: 1) list of sub-processors handling EU tenant traffic 2) can we guarantee no cross-border egress without written consent 3) how certs/TLS are managed and whether mutual TLS is available 4) does egress to non-EU providers occur for analytics/monitoring 5) any per-GB egress pricing or add-on for geofencing.
Ben (Solutions): Got it. Short answers first: sub-processors list is maintained in our public SOC2 page (link) but infra details below. We do allow optional mTLS for Dedicated/Private. Hosted uses TLS1.3 to edge + internal TLS between services; by default telemetry goes to our EU telemetry endpoint, but some third-party monitoring (CDN, logging) can be outside EU unless pinned. Need infra to confirm exact egress flows for Hosted.
Carlos (Eng-Infra): TL;DR: For EU-hosted tenants on Hosted API, primary data-inference path is within the chosen EU region (e.g., eu-west-1). Certificate/transport details: we terminate client TLS at the regional edge (TLS1.2/1.3), backend segments use mTLS between services. We support client mTLS via customer cert upload for Dedicated and Private; Hosted does not support client-supplied mTLS today. Sub-processors: AWS GCP (regional), our CDN partner (FastEdge EU POPs), and a managed logging provider (LogVault EU cluster). All of those have EU-resident clusters for EU tenants by default.
Carlos (Eng-Infra): Caveats: 1) DNS lookups/health checks may hit global resolvers — no customer data in payloads but IPs may be outside EU 2) In Hosted, some background analytics/aggregates are routed to a centralized metrics cluster in us-central for cross-region ops — we can opt to replicate metrics to EU-only for this FinBank POC but it requires a config change and a 30d lead time 3) If customer enables certain features (e.g., automatic model-updates via external fetchers), those fetchers reach out to public model registries which may be outside EU.
Sam (AE): Important — customer insists on "no cross-border egress without written consent." Can Legal confirm what we can contractually commit to?
Dana (Legal): We can contractually commit for Hosted to keep inference payloads within EU regional clusters and to restrict sub-processors to EU-resident instances where available. However, we need to scope exceptions: DNS, global auth tokens, and optional managed services. Suggest: 1) create a Residency Addendum that lists allowed exceptions 2) require a written change request for any future cross-border egress. I can draft language if we decide to offer EU-only telemetry for them.
Vivian (Sales Ops): Pricing note: If we enable EU-only telemetry + replicate metrics to EU, that's an ops delta. Recommend quoting as "EU residency addon" — one-time onboarding fee + monthly egress replication charge. Typical numbers: onboarding ~$5k, replication egress ~€0.02/GB (approx). For strict geofence pinning to Dedicated, add a capacity reservation premium (~15%). I'll validate numbers with finance but want to flag.
Ben (Solutions): Thanks. To unblock the customer now, they also asked for a short runbook they can hand to their security team. I can draft — Carlos, can you confirm the micro-steps we should include for Hosted -> EU-only?
Carlos (Eng-Infra): Runbook snippet (can paste to customer):
```
1) Customer signs Residency Addendum
2) We enable EU regional pin for tenant (provision ~4h)
3) Flip telemetry replication to EU-only (requires 30d lead time if not pre-provisioned)
4) Verify endpoints: api.eu.redwood.ai and metrics.eu.redwood.ai
5) Whitelist Regional IP ranges (we provide CIDR list) and confirm egress rules
6) Optional: migrate to Dedicated (if mTLS / private certs required)
```
Carlos (Eng-Infra): Also add: Provide list of sub-processors + their EU region locations (I will export and attach).
Sam (AE): Perfect. Dana — can you draft the Residency Addendum language we discussed? Need quick turnaround — customer legal is strict.
Dana (Legal): I'll draft a short addendum with exceptions enumerated. ETA EOD tomorrow.
Vivian (Sales Ops): I'll prep a quote with three lines: Hosted + EU residency addon, Dedicated pin (capacity premium), and Private deployment option. Will include estimated onboarding + monthly egress delta.
ops-bot: Incident: none — automated check of regional IPs completed OK for eu-west-1 (no known leaks). :white_check_mark:
Ben (Solutions): Next actions: Sam to send customer the runbook + note that Legal will follow with addendum; Vivian to attach draft pricing; Carlos to drop the subprocessor export in this thread when ready.
Sam (AE): Thanks all — I'll send an initial reply to the customer with the runbook and set expectation for Legal/Quote followups. :thumbsup:
